announcements: NEW: The IBM PC Users Forum is now open -- GO IBMPC. Share configuration tips and software notes for the new IBM Personal Computer.
CB Simulator: Channel 12 is reserved for IBM PC discussion this weekend. All handles welcome.
Scheduled maintenance: the service will be unavailable Sunday 2:00-6:00 AM Eastern for system upgrades.
cb_topics: Anybody else see the IBM announcement? $1565 for 16K. SIXTEEN K.
My TRS-80 has more memory than that base model, and I paid less in '79.
VisiCalc on an IBM. That is the whole ballgame for business users.
CP/M-86 costs how much more than DOS? Kildall must be fuming.
Gas is over a buck thirty here. Remember when it was fifty cents?
Who is watching Dallas this fall? Sue Ellen had better behave.

headlines.summary: IBM announced its smallest, lowest-priced computer, the IBM Personal Computer, at a New York press conference this morning. The base system, with 16K of memory and BASIC built in, sells for $1,565 through ComputerLand dealers, Sears business machine stores, and IBM sales centers.
headlines.title: IBM ENTERS PERSONAL COMPUTER MARKET

headlines.summary: The system uses an Intel 8088 processor running at 4.77 megahertz. Buyers may choose PC-DOS from Microsoft for $40, CP/M-86 from Digital Research, or the UCSD p-System. VisiCalc and Peachtree business software were named among the programs available at launch.
headlines.title: NEW IBM MACHINE RUNS MICROSOFT DOS

headlines.summary: Byte magazine called the machine 'one of the most important announcements we have seen in the industry.' Apple answered with a full-page Wall Street Journal advertisement reading 'Welcome, IBM. Seriously,' welcoming the giant to the personal computer business.
headlines.title: INDUSTRY REACTS TO IBM ANNOUNCEMENT

headlines.summary: Breaking with its closed-system tradition, IBM is publishing a Technical Reference manual with BIOS listings and expansion schematics, and will sell its own line of plug-in expansion boards for the new machine.
headlines.title: IBM OPENS MACHINE TO DEVELOPERS

headlines.summary: Congress has sent the President the Economic Recovery Tax Act, the largest tax cut in American history, calling for a 25 percent across-the-board reduction phased in over three years. Signing is expected this week at his California ranch.
headlines.title: REAGAN TAX CUT AWAITS PRESIDENT'S SIGNATURE

headlines.summary: More than 11,000 air traffic controllers remain off the job after President Reagan ordered striking PATCO members fired last week. Military controllers and supervisors are handling commercial traffic, and airlines are flying reduced schedules.
headlines.title: AIR CONTROLLERS STRIKE ENTERS SECOND WEEK

headlines.summary: Major league baseball resumed this week after a 50-day players' strike, with the All-Star Game played Sunday in Cleveland. Owners and players agreed to a split-season format with an extra round of playoffs.
headlines.title: BASEBALL BACK AFTER PLAYERS' STRIKE

headlines.summary: MTV: Music Television began cablecasting August 1 with the Buggles' 'Video Killed the Radio Star.' The Warner-Amex channel programs rock videos around the clock.
headlines.title: CABLE VIEWERS GET ALL-MUSIC CHANNEL

headlines.summary: Solidarity, the independent Polish labor federation, continues pressing the Warsaw government for economic reforms amid food shortages and labor unrest.
headlines.title: POLISH UNION PRESSURES WARSAW GOVERNMENT

headlines.summary: The Federal Reserve's tight-money campaign keeps the prime lending rate near 20 percent as the central bank battles double-digit inflation. Business borrowing costs remain at historic highs.
headlines.title: PRIME RATE HOLDS NEAR 20 PERCENT

1981-08-12.label: IBM PC announced
market_notes: Prime rate near 20% as Volcker's Federal Reserve squeezes inflation; business borrowing at historic cost.
IBM shares watched closely after the PC announcement; analysts debate whether Big Blue can move fast in the microcomputer market.

on_this_day.summary: MTV: Music Television began cablecasting with 'Video Killed the Radio Star.'
on_this_day.title: MTV signs on (August 1, 1981)

on_this_day.summary: PATCO members strike; President Reagan orders strikers fired.
on_this_day.title: Air traffic controllers walk out (August 3, 1981)

on_this_day.summary: IBM announces the Model 5150 at $1,565, entering the microcomputer market.
on_this_day.title: IBM introduces the Personal Computer (August 12, 1981)

announcements: NEW: The Macintosh Owners Forum is now open -- GO MAC. Tips, desk accessories, and software notes for Apple's new machine.
The '1984' ad got you curious? Our Apple SIG has Macintosh technical threads starting today.
CB Simulator: Channel 8 is the unofficial Macintosh channel. Mouse users welcome.
cb_topics: The Mac talked! Did anyone else read about the shareholders meeting?
$2495 for 128K and no hard disk. My PC-XT laughs.
A mouse. Icons. No more DOS commands to memorize. My wife could use this.
That 1984 commercial during the Super Bowl -- the hammer throw! Best ad ever.
Raiders killed the Redskins. 38-9. Marcus Allen is unreal.
Long distance is a mess since the breakup. MCI keeps calling me at dinner.

headlines.summary: Apple Computer introduced the Macintosh at its annual shareholders meeting in Cupertino today. The $2,495 machine replaces typed commands with a mouse, icons, and pull-down menus on a 9-inch black-and-white display.
headlines.title: APPLE UNVEILS MACINTOSH

headlines.summary: In a flourish, Steven Jobs had the machine introduce itself in synthesized speech before a cheering audience: 'Never trust a computer you can't lift!' The demonstration drew a standing ovation.
headlines.title: 'HELLO, I'M MACINTOSH'

headlines.summary: Motorola 68000 processor at 8 megahertz, 128K of memory, a 3.5-inch 400K floppy drive, and bundled MacWrite and MacPaint software. There is no hard disk; a second floppy drive is optional.
headlines.title: MACINTOSH SPECIFICATIONS DETAILED

headlines.summary: Two days before the unveiling, Apple's Ridley Scott-directed '1984' commercial aired during Super Bowl XVIII. The Los Angeles Raiders defeated Washington 38-9 at Tampa Stadium before more than 77 million viewers.
headlines.title: APPLE'S '1984' AD STUNS SUPER BOWL VIEWERS

headlines.summary: The AT&T divestiture became effective January 1, spinning off seven regional Bell companies. Long-distance customers are choosing among AT&T, MCI, and Sprint for the first time.
headlines.title: BELL SYSTEM BREAKUP TAKES EFFECT

headlines.summary: U.S. Marines remain at the Beirut airport as part of the multinational force, months after the October barracks bombing killed 241 American servicemen.
headlines.title: MARINES HOLD BEIRUT POSITIONS

headlines.summary: Astronomers are preparing for Halley's Comet, due at perihelion in February 1986, with an international armada of spacecraft planned for close encounters.
headlines.title: ASTRONOMERS AWAIT HALLEY'S COMET

headlines.summary: Marcus Allen ran for 191 yards and two touchdowns as Los Angeles won 38-9 at Tampa Stadium on Sunday, the most lopsided Super Bowl yet played.
headlines.title: RAIDERS ROUT REDSKINS IN SUPER BOWL

headlines.summary: The spreadsheet program remains the must-have business application, moving IBM-compatible hardware off dealer shelves as offices automate.
headlines.title: LOTUS 1-2-3 DRIVES PC SALES

headlines.summary: The Yugoslavian city is readying venues for the Winter Olympics, opening February 8 with athletes from dozens of nations.
headlines.title: SARAJEVO PREPARES FOR WINTER GAMES

1984-01-24.label: Apple Macintosh debuts
market_notes: Apple shares in focus after the Macintosh unveiling; analysts split on whether $2,495 is too rich for the home market.
AT&T begins life as a long-distance company; the seven regional Bells open separately. Dividend checks will look different this quarter.

on_this_day.summary: The Ridley Scott spot runs during Super Bowl XVIII.
on_this_day.title: Apple's '1984' commercial airs (January 22, 1984)

on_this_day.summary: The Bell System splits into AT&T and seven regional companies.
on_this_day.title: AT&T divestiture takes effect (January 1, 1984)

on_this_day.summary: James Marshall's find sets off the California Gold Rush.
on_this_day.title: Gold discovered at Sutter's Mill (January 24, 1848)

announcements: A message from the sysops: our thoughts are with the families of the Challenger crew, and with the teachers and students who followed this mission. Tonight's CB conference will observe a moment of silence.
The Space/Astronomy forum has opened a memorial thread for Challenger. Please keep discussion respectful.
NASA mission summaries are being added to the reference library as they become available.
cb_topics: I watched it happen live. My kids' classroom went silent. I do not have words.
Christa McAuliffe was supposed to teach lessons from orbit. My daughter wrote her a letter.
Reagan speaks tonight. 'Slipped the surly bonds of earth.' I am not ashamed to say I cried.
The Bears won the Super Bowl Sunday. Feels like a month ago already.
Does anyone know if the shuttle program will fly again? My son keeps asking.
Gas is under a dollar here for the first time in years. Small mercies.

headlines.summary: The space shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff from Kennedy Space Center this morning, killing all seven aboard. The crew included Christa McAuliffe, the New Hampshire teacher chosen as the first private citizen in space.
headlines.title: SHUTTLE CHALLENGER LOST AFTER LIFTOFF

headlines.summary: The President set aside tonight's address to Congress, declaring 'today is a day for mourning and remembering,' and will speak to the nation from the Oval Office this evening.
headlines.title: REAGAN POSTPONES STATE OF THE UNION

headlines.summary: Commander Francis Scobee, pilot Michael Smith, mission specialists Judith Resnik, Ellison Onizuka and Ronald McNair, and payload specialists Gregory Jarvis and Christa McAuliffe.
headlines.title: THE CREW OF STS-51L

headlines.summary: The launch went ahead despite overnight temperatures near freezing, the coldest shuttle launch yet. NASA officials say it is too early to know whether the cold played a role; a board of inquiry is being appointed.
headlines.title: QUESTIONS ABOUT COLD-WEATHER LAUNCH

headlines.summary: Millions of schoolchildren watched live as McAuliffe, 37, a social studies teacher from Concord, New Hampshire, was to teach two lessons from orbit during the mission.
headlines.title: SCHOOLS MOURN TEACHER IN SPACE

headlines.summary: Chicago defeated New England 46-10 Sunday at the Superdome, capping a dominant season. William 'The Refrigerator' Perry scored a touchdown.
headlines.title: BEARS CRUSH PATRIOTS IN SUPER BOWL

headlines.summary: The comet reaches its closest approach to the sun next month; spacecraft from the Soviet Union, Japan, and Europe are closing in for encounters.
headlines.title: HALLEY'S COMET NEARS PERIHELION

headlines.summary: Crude oil continues its slide as OPEC members pump beyond quotas, squeezing Texas producers and alarming energy lenders.
headlines.title: OIL PRICES SLIDE BELOW $20

headlines.summary: Corazon Aquino is drawing large crowds challenging Ferdinand Marcos ahead of next month's snap presidential election.
headlines.title: AQUINO CAMPAIGNS IN PHILIPPINES

headlines.summary: Apple's LaserWriter printer and Aldus PageMaker software are bringing typeset-quality pages to desktop Macintoshes, creating a new category of business computing.
headlines.title: DESKTOP PUBLISHING GROWS

1986-01-28.label: Challenger
market_notes: Oil's slide continues; crude under $20 pressures energy stocks and Texas banks.
Defense and aerospace shares steady; investors await NASA's inquiry before reassessing shuttle contractors.

on_this_day.summary: Chicago defeats New England 46-10 at the Superdome.
on_this_day.title: Chicago Bears win Super Bowl XX (January 26, 1986)

on_this_day.summary: New Haven, Connecticut, switches on the first telephone exchange.
on_this_day.title: First commercial telephone exchange opens (January 28, 1878)

on_this_day.summary: STS-51L breaks apart 73 seconds after liftoff; seven crew members killed.
on_this_day.title: Space Shuttle Challenger lost (January 28, 1986)

announcements: Market data services are experiencing extremely heavy volume today. Quotes may be delayed; thank you for your patience.
The Investors Forum has opened a special thread on today's market action -- GO INVESTORS.
Scheduled maintenance remains set for Sunday 2:00-6:00 AM Eastern.
cb_topics: The Dow just fell 500 points. FIVE HUNDRED. Is my 401(k) gone?
My broker's line has been busy for two hours. TWO HOURS.
They are saying the computers did it -- program trading just kept selling.
And on the same day we are shelling Iranian oil platforms. What a Monday.
Twins are up 2-0 in the Series, at least. Small comfort.
My dad says he remembers '29. He says do not panic. Trying not to.

headlines.summary: The Dow Jones industrial average fell 508.32 points, or 22.6 percent, to 1,738.74 -- the largest one-day decline in Wall Street history, nearly double the 1929 record. A record 604 million shares changed hands.
headlines.title: DOW PLUNGES 508 POINTS IN HISTORIC CRASH

headlines.summary: Order systems were overwhelmed as the selloff accelerated; dozens of stocks faced delayed openings, and investors waited an hour or more for trade confirmations.
headlines.title: SELLING SWAMPS EXCHANGE SYSTEMS

headlines.summary: Computer-driven portfolio insurance strategies are blamed for accelerating the decline, turning a selloff into a cascade as programs dumped stock-index futures automatically.
headlines.title: PROGRAM TRADING BLAMED FOR CASCADE

headlines.summary: Panic circled the globe as exchanges from Hong Kong to London to Sydney posted heavy losses, with London's market suffering its worst week on record.
headlines.title: CRASH GOES GLOBAL

headlines.summary: The White House said the economy remains fundamentally sound. Treasury and Federal Reserve officials are in close contact as markets reel, and traders await word on emergency measures.
headlines.title: WASHINGTON RESPONDS TO MELTDOWN

headlines.summary: Navy warships shelled two Iranian oil platforms in the Persian Gulf in retaliation for last week's missile attack on the reflagged tanker Sea Isle City. President Reagan called it 'a prudent yet restrained response.'
headlines.title: U.S. DESTROYS IRANIAN OIL PLATFORMS

headlines.summary: Treasury Secretary James Baker's weekend threat to let the dollar fall further, after criticizing West Germany's interest-rate hike, deepened fears of a policy rift days before the crash.
headlines.title: BAKER'S DOLLAR REMARKS RATTLE MARKETS

headlines.summary: U.S. and Soviet negotiators are pressing toward an intermediate-range missile treaty ahead of a planned December summit between Reagan and Gorbachev.
headlines.title: ARMS TALKS PRESS TOWARD SUMMIT

headlines.summary: Minnesota took the first two games at the Metrodome over St. Louis; the Series resumes Tuesday night in Missouri.
headlines.title: TWINS LEAD WORLD SERIES 2-0

headlines.summary: IBM's PS/2 line, introduced this spring with the OS/2 operating system, faces a cautious market as businesses weigh the cost of upgrading.
headlines.title: IBM'S PS/2 FACES SKEPTICAL MARKET

headlines.summary: Brokerage phone lines jammed as individual investors tried to reach advisors, and mutual fund redemption orders piled up through the afternoon.
headlines.title: BROKERS SWAMPED BY WORRIED CALLERS

headlines.summary: Candidates are campaigning ahead of December's presidential election, the country's first direct vote in 16 years.
headlines.title: SOUTH KOREA CAMPAIGNS FOR DECEMBER VOTE

1987-10-19.label: Black Monday
market_notes: Volume: 604.3 million shares, triple the daily average; dozens of NYSE trading delays and halts.
An estimated $500+ billion in NYSE market value erased in a single session.
Portfolio insurance and program trading identified as accelerants; dollar policy and trade-deficit fears as triggers.

on_this_day.summary: The British surrender effectively ends the American Revolutionary War.
on_this_day.title: Cornwallis surrenders at Yorktown (October 19, 1781)

on_this_day.summary: The Grande Armee turns back toward France as winter closes in.
on_this_day.title: Napoleon begins retreat from Moscow (October 19, 1812)

on_this_day.summary: The largest one-day percentage drop in Wall Street history.
on_this_day.title: Dow falls 508 points (October 19, 1987)

announcements: The International News forum has an open thread on events in Berlin. Please keep discussion civil -- GO WORLDNEWS.
CB Simulator: Channel 1 is hosting an open discussion on tonight's events in Germany. All members welcome.
New in the reference library: a Germany fact file with maps of Berlin's crossing points.
cb_topics: Are you watching Berlin? People are standing ON the Wall. ON it.
My cousin was stationed in West Berlin in the 70s. He says he is crying.
Schabowski just... announced it by accident? Unbelievable.
Wilder won in Virginia and Dinkins in New York. What a week.
My kid wants a Game Boy for Christmas. So does every kid in America.
The A's swept the Series and now this. October and November have been unreal.

headlines.summary: East German authorities announced this evening that citizens may travel to the West effective immediately. Thousands massed at border crossings in Berlin, and overwhelmed guards opened the gates. Crowds are celebrating atop the Wall tonight.
headlines.title: EAST GERMANY OPENS THE WALL

headlines.summary: Politburo spokesman Guenter Schabowski, handed new travel regulations he had not been briefed on, told a televised press conference the rules take effect 'immediately, without delay.' Within the hour, East Berliners were streaming toward the crossings.
headlines.title: SCHABOWSKI ANNOUNCEMENT IGNITES EXODUS

headlines.summary: Border guards, who had received no clear orders, yielded to the crowds late in the evening as chants of 'Open the gate!' rose at checkpoints across the divided city.
headlines.title: CROSSINGS OVERWHELMED LATE TONIGHT

headlines.summary: President Bush welcomed the development but struck a cautious note, saying he would not 'dance on the Berlin Wall.' In Moscow, Soviet officials offered no objection as the night unfolded.
headlines.title: BUSH WELCOMES OPENING, URGES CALM

headlines.summary: In Tuesday's elections, L. Douglas Wilder became the first elected black governor in American history in Virginia, and David Dinkins became New York City's first black mayor.
headlines.title: WILDER, DINKINS MAKE HISTORY IN U.S. VOTE

headlines.summary: European markets took the Berlin news in stride; analysts are weighing what open borders and reunification talk mean for the continent's economy.
headlines.title: MARKETS STEADY AS EUROPE SHIFTS

headlines.summary: Nintendo's handheld, launched in the U.S. this summer with Tetris packed in, is the season's must-have toy as the holidays approach.
headlines.title: GAME BOY CONQUERS PLAYGROUNDS

headlines.summary: The Bay Area continues cleanup from the October 17 Loma Prieta earthquake, which killed 63 people and collapsed a section of the Bay Bridge.
headlines.title: QUAKE RECOVERY CONTINUES IN CALIFORNIA

headlines.summary: Oakland completed a four-game sweep of San Francisco in the World Series, played ten days late after the earthquake interrupted it.
headlines.title: A'S SWEEP GIANTS IN QUAKE-DELAYED SERIES

headlines.summary: The Galileo spacecraft, launched last month aboard the shuttle Atlantis, is on its six-year voyage to Jupiter.
headlines.title: GALILEO EN ROUTE TO JUPITER

1989-11-09.label: Berlin Wall falls
market_notes: West German markets steady; traders debate what open borders mean for European growth.
U.S. markets little changed; analysts say the week's U.S. election results matter more to domestic stocks.

on_this_day.summary: Anti-Jewish violence erupts across Germany; synagogues and shops destroyed.
on_this_day.title: Kristallnacht pogroms begin (November 9, 1938)

on_this_day.summary: A massive power failure darkens New York and much of the Northeast.
on_this_day.title: Northeast blackout (November 9, 1965)

on_this_day.summary: East Germany announces free travel; crowds stream through the crossings.
on_this_day.title: Berlin Wall opened (November 9, 1989)

announcements: NEW: The Internet SIG is now open -- GO INTERNET. Discussion of TCP/IP tools, Gopher, and the new WorldWideWeb project from CERN.
The file library has a new Internet section with FTP site lists and protocol documents.
CB Simulator: Channel 9 hosts a weekly Internet roundtable, Thursdays at 9 PM Eastern.
cb_topics: Some fellow at CERN posted about a 'WorldWideWeb.' Hypertext over the Internet. Anyone tried it?
You need a NeXT to run his browser. A NeXT! Who has ten grand?
Gopher is easier. Menus, no fancy formatting. This web thing is a toy.
START treaty signed. Maybe the Cold War is really over.
Terminator 2 last month -- the liquid metal fellow. Best effects I have ever seen.
Gas is $1.14 here and I am supposed to be happy about it?

headlines.summary: Tim Berners-Lee, a computer scientist at CERN in Geneva, posted a public invitation on the alt.hypertext newsgroup today describing the WorldWideWeb project: a hypertext system for sharing information across the Internet. The first site runs on his NeXT computer at info.cern.ch.
headlines.title: CERN PHYSICIST INVITES WORLD TO 'WEB'

headlines.summary: Berners-Lee's system links documents with hypertext using new protocols called HTTP and HTML. Readers need his WorldWideWeb browser program, now publicly available, to follow the links between documents.
headlines.title: WHAT IS THE WORLDWIDEWEB?

headlines.summary: The University of Minnesota's Gopher protocol, released this spring, offers a simpler, menu-driven rival for finding information on the Internet -- and currently has far more users than the new Web.
headlines.title: GOPHER OFFERS MENU-DRIVEN RIVAL

headlines.summary: Presidents Bush and Gorbachev signed the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty last week in Moscow, limiting each side to 6,000 nuclear warheads. The Senate must still ratify it.
headlines.title: START TREATY SIGNED IN MOSCOW

headlines.summary: Soviet conservatives are criticizing Gorbachev's reforms as the republics press for sovereignty, raising questions about the reformer's hold on power.
headlines.title: GORBACHEV FACES HARD-LINE PRESSURE

headlines.summary: Unemployment remains above 6.5 percent as the nation waits to see whether the recession that began last summer has truly ended.
headlines.title: ECONOMY SHOWS MIXED SIGNALS

headlines.summary: With two months to play, division races are tightening across both leagues as contenders jockey for October.
headlines.title: BASEBALL PENNANT RACES TIGHTEN

headlines.summary: Microsoft's latest DOS adds task swapping, an improved BASIC, and a full-screen editor, with upgrade pricing under $100.
headlines.title: MS-DOS 5.0 SHIPS TO DEALERS

headlines.summary: Clarence Thomas's Supreme Court nomination awaits fall confirmation hearings after his July selection to replace Thurgood Marshall.
headlines.title: THOMAS NOMINATION AWAITS FALL HEARINGS

headlines.summary: Astronomers are designing corrective optics for the Hubble Space Telescope's flawed mirror, with a shuttle repair mission planned for the coming years.
headlines.title: HUBBLE TEAMS PLAN MIRROR REPAIR

1991-08-06.label: first website public invitation
market_notes: Stocks drift as investors parse mixed economic data; unemployment stuck above 6.5%.
Technology shares mixed; Microsoft's DOS 5.0 launch draws dealer interest.

on_this_day.summary: The first combat use of an atomic weapon devastates the Japanese city.
on_this_day.title: Atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima (August 6, 1945)

on_this_day.summary: The Security Council imposes sweeping sanctions after the invasion of Kuwait.
on_this_day.title: U.N. sanctions Iraq (August 6, 1990)

on_this_day.summary: Tim Berners-Lee posts a public invitation to the Web project on alt.hypertext.
on_this_day.title: WorldWideWeb opened to the public (August 6, 1991)
